subject: A start on multiple proposals on same project

messages.author: ec32e5a92a275a89
messages.subject: A start on multiple proposals on same project
parts:
We've lots of project proposals, and some are multiples.

I am nominal mentor for two projects -- optimgui and convex optimization. For myself, I
plan over the weekend to

1) list the proposals under each project using surname of author

2) For each project, rank the proposals, 1 for first, 2 second, etc.

3) Try to suggest which, if any, should be dropped from consideration. I am fairly certain
at least 1 will get dropped, and in any event, the mentor's view should be useful to
others, so I'll post the ranking and suggestion to drop as a private comment on each of
the proposals in a project set.

Can I ask others with multiple candidates to do something similar?

I'll then see if we can reach consensus on proposals that we can drop from further
consideration of this type.

I'd also welcome suggestions on which other weak proposals to eliminate from consideration
early so we can focus on the stronger ones. There is a button (possibly only for admins)
to "Ignore this proposal". However, I'm not sure what is the most efficient way to do
this. Possibly via a private comment on the weak proposals in the form

youremail student_name (brief reason why weak)

that I can consolidate into a small spreadsheet to see what consensus we have. The Melange
approach tries to force things to a single numerical scoring and could result in us having
a very poor mix of recommended proposals. I'd very much like to see us put reasons down.

As it is very easy to inadvertently share comments intended to be private, please be
measured in language, even if the comments are necessarily negative.

Best,

JN

messages.author: 29bcefae00c9a0bb
messages.subject: RE: A start on multiple proposals on same project
parts:
Are you suggesting that the primary mentor for each project do this preliminary screening/ranking for his/her project?

In my case, I have one project: Accelerators for EM/MM algorithms. I think it has received the largest # of applicants (7), if I am not mistaken.

Would you like me to rank these 7 proposals, as well as indicate if and why any of the bottom-ranked ones are weak? Of course, if there are no "weak" ones then just the ranking would be provided (possibly with ties). Am I correctly understanding you?

Ravi.
